'''Billy Garrett Jr.''' (born October 16, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[CD Estela]] of the [[Primera FEB]]. He played briefly in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) for the [[New York Knicks]]. He has also played professionally in the [[NBA G League]] as well as for teams in several international leagues. His professional highlights include a G League Championship in 2021 with the [[Lakeland Magic]] and [[All-PLK Team]] recognition in 2022.

Garrett Jr. played college basketball for [[DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball|DePaul]], where he holds the record for career [[free throw]]s made. He was the 2014 [[Big East Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year]] and earned several collegiate honors for his performance in the classroom and in the community. In high school Garrett Jr. played for [[Morgan Park High School]] where he won [[Chicago Public High School League]] (CPL) and [[Illinois High School Association]] (IHSA) championships.

Garrett was the first person known to be afflicted with [[sickle cell disease]] to become an NBA player and has been an advocate and public speaker for the cause. Garrett is the grandson of [[Bill Garrett (basketball)|Bill Garrett]], who integrated [[Big Ten]] basketball.

==High school career==
Billy Garrett Jr. is the son of Billy Garrett Sr. and Annissa Lambrith-Garrett.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.depaulbluedemons.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/billy_garrett_jr_851112.html|title=5-BILLY GARRETT JR.|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215221425/http://www.depaulbluedemons.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/billy_garrett_jr_851112.html |archive-date=2017-12-15 }}</ref> As a youth, Garrett Jr. played basketball, [[baseball]] and [[American football]].<ref name="si"/> Garrett's grandfather was [[Bill Garrett (basketball)|Bill Garrett]], the first African-American basketball player in the [[Big Ten]].<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/more-sports/2012/07/17/billy-garrett-jr|title=Billy Garrett Jr. follows family's example in fight against sickle cell|access-date=May 7, 2019|date=July 17, 2012|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|author=Dauster, Rob}}</ref> The younger Garrett attended [[Morgan Park High School]]. He committed to DePaul early in his high school career.<ref name="tide">{{cite news|last1=Helfgot|first1=Mike|title=DePaul preview: Billy Garrett Jr. has one more go-round to turn losing tide|url=http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/ct-billy-garrett-depaul-basketball-preview-spt-1111-20161110-story.html|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=November 10, 2016}}</ref> Garrett achieved basketball success despite being "The only [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] basketball player afflicted with the "SC" form of [[sickle cell disease]]".<ref name="haugh">{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1648034881|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1648034881}}|title=Beating tough odds is in Garrett's blood: Sickle cell disease can't derail DePaul sophomore|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Haugh, David|access-date=March 22, 2024|date=January 26, 2015|page=1|quote=}}</ref>

===Freshman season (2009–10)===
Before Garrett Jr.'s high school freshman season during the 2009 summer, his father, Billy Garrett Sr., was hired as an assistant coach at DePaul, and Garrett Sr. survived the 2010 transition from [[Jerry Wainwright]] to [[Oliver Purnell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/418002366|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|418002366}}|title=Purnell's 1st calls are local: Reaches out to city HS coaches on 1st day on job|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=April 8, 2010|page=2.3|quote=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/420860223|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|420860223}}|title=Demons have work to do in city: Public League not yet embracing staff|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=April 22, 2010|page=5|quote=}}</ref> As a freshman during the 2010 [[Chicago Public High School League]], championship tournament, Garrett Jr. played well enough at times that defenses opted not to double-team [[Wayne Blackshear]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/420720704|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|420720704}}|title=Growth spurt has powered Mustangs: Morgan Park rose to occasion with Blackshear hobbled|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=February 19, 2010|page=2.8|quote=Guards Markee Williams, Andre Hall, Billy Garrett and Leron Smith did a lot of damage in second- and quarterfinal-round upsets of Young and Simeon, so much so that Hyde Park played Blackshear straight up, without weakside help for most of the game.}}</ref> The team went on to win the 2010 city championship over [[Marshall Metropolitan High School]], with notable contributions from its freshman guards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/246909906|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|246909906}}|title=Morgan Park tops Marshall|work=[[Chicago Defender]]|author=Thomas, Todd|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=February 24, 2010|page=38|quote=Freshman guards Markee Williams and Billy Garrett Jr. also played well in the championship game and the entire city playoffs.}}</ref>

===Sophomore season (2010–11)===
As a sophomore, he was expected to continue to perform at a high enough level to "take some pressure off of Wayne Blackshear" when the ''[[Chicago Tribune]]'' ranked them as the number three team the [[Chicago metropolitan area]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/808469371|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|808469371}}|title=TRIBUNE'S PRESEASON TOP 20|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=November 24, 2010|page=8|quote=}}</ref> That year they found themselves matched up against a [[Jabari Parker]]-led [[Simeon Career Academy]] that was ranked number 3 in the nation by ''[[USA Today]]'' and number 1 in the state in the CPL championship second round, where they lost 52–45.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/851222779|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|851222779}}|title=BOYS BASKETBALL SIMEON 52, MORGAN PARK 45: Mustangs fail to corral Parker|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=February 11, 2011|page=2.6|quote=}}</ref> In the 2011 IHSA Class 3A sectional semifinal against [[Hillcrest High School (Country Club Hills, Illinois)|Hillcrest High School]], Garrett scored 20 points, including 10 in the second quarter to help rally Morgan park from a 27–18 deficit.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/856162456|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|856162456}}|title=Mustangs KO champs: Blackshear gets plenty of help; MORGAN PARK 80, HILLCREST 76|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=March 10, 2011|page=6|quote=}}</ref> Following the season, Garrett Jr. committed to DePaul.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/860868072|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|860868072}}|title=IN BRIEF|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=April 8, 2011|page=11|quote=}}</ref> At that time, he was ranked as the 7th best Chicago-area and 8th best Illinois recruit in the national class of 2013 as the number 92-ranked prospect.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/868372786|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|868372786}}|title=5-7 Randolph not short on skill, will|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=May 25, 2011|page=2.7|quote=}}</ref>

===Junior season (2011–12)===
When [[Wayne Blackshear]] graduated in 2011, Garrett became the focal point of the team as a junior.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/chicago/high-school/post/_/id/2204/top-20-boys-basketball-preview|title=Top 20 boys basketball preview|access-date=May 7, 2019|date=November 21, 2011|publisher=[[ESPN]]|author=Powers, Scott}}</ref> He entered his junior season ranked by the ''Chicago Tribune'' as fifth among area players to watch.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/910153728|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|910153728}}|title=2011-12 BOYS BASKETBALL PREVIEW: Baller ID; Who will be the stars of March?|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Discher, Emilia|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=November 10, 2011|page=10|quote=}}</ref> When Mac Irvin, "known as the 'Godfather' of Chicago basketball" died from [[diabetes]] complications in December 2011, Garrett Jr. delivered a [[eulogy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/912807358|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|912807358}}|title='He was the backbone': Loss of Mac Irvin makes win tough for Morgan Park|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=December 28, 2011|page=6|quote=}}</ref> At the time, Garrett Jr. was described as a [[point guard]] in a [[shooting guard]]'s body.<ref name=HPslog>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/911147098|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|911147098}}|title=Hyde Park still leaning on guard: No transfer of leadership for Thunderbirds|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=December 16, 2011|page=6|quote=}}</ref> In the December 2011 Proviso West Tournament, he posted 30 points in a 50–41 loss to [[New Trier High School]] on December 29.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/913025214|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|913025214}}|title=2 better than just 1: New Trier pair offset Garrett's 30 to reach final; NEW TRIER 50, MORGAN PARK 41|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=December 30, 2011|page=9|quote=}}</ref> That season he was the only underclassman recognized as a 2012 [[Associated Press]] boys basketball Class 3A all-state first team selection (in a year where the Associated Press named several future NBA talents to its Class 4A first team — [[Jabari Parker]], [[Fred VanVleet]] and [[Malcolm Hill (basketball)|Malcolm Hill]] — and second team — [[Jahlil Okafor]] and [[Kendrick Nunn]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/935563176|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|935563176}}|title=Boys basketball|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=March 15, 2012|page=7|quote=}}</ref> The ''Chicago Tribune'' named him third team All-state along with [[Sterling Brown (basketball)|Sterling Brown]], [[Milton Doyle]], Tony Hicks and Rashaun Stimage.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/963385476|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|963385476}}|title=MR. BASKETBALL OF ILLINOIS: JABARI PARKER, SIMEON: Junior giant; 4A champions' superstar earns place in history|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=April 1, 2012|page=11|quote=}}</ref> He finished the year as the sixth rated national class of 2013 recruit in Illinois at number 75 according to [[Rivals.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1011655105|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1011655105}}|title=Illini must spread net|work=[[News Gazette]]|author=Tate, Loren|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=April 29, 2012|page=C.2|quote=}}</ref>

===Senior season (2012–13)===
[[File:20130316 IHSA 3A championship game Billy Garrett (2).jpg|thumb|upright|left|Garrett for [[Morgan Park High School]] in the 2013 [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] 3A championship game.]]
Garrett entered his senior season as the 17th ranked point guard in the national class of 2013, according to [[Scout.com]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1151905030|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1151905030}}|title=Jackson big gem for Irish: Point guard leads 14th-ranked class|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Hamilton, Brian|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=November 15, 2012|page=3.3|quote=}}</ref> His backup was {{height|ft=5|in=9}} freshman [[Charlie Moore (basketball)|Charlie Moore]], who entered the season rated as one of the top 5 underclassmen in the Chicago area and with [[NCAA Division I]] offers from [[Bradley Braves men's basketball|Bradley]] and [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1179268805|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1179268805}}|title=TOP 5 UNDERCLASSMEN|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=November 22, 2012|page=7|quote=}}</ref> That season {{height|ft=6|in=0}} [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] recruit Kyle Davis, who had been described as a [[shooting guard]] in a [[point guard]]'s body,<ref name=HPslog/> transferred from [[Hyde Park Academy High School]] to complement the {{height|ft=6|in=5}} Garrett.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1242008980|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1242008980}}|title=Morgan Park duo finding rhythm: Guards Davis, Garrett get their games to match|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 25, 2024|date=December 21, 2012|page=8|quote=}}</ref> 

Morgan Park's only loss in the 2012 portion of their schedule was at the hands of the sophomore season [[Stephen Zimmerman]]-led [[Bishop Gorman High School]] in an 83–80 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] loss at the Tarkanian Classic in [[Las Vegas]] on December 21. Zimmerman tallied 24 points, 8 rebounds and 3 blocked shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1243010649|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1243010649}}|title=Size advantage proves pivotal for Liberty|work=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]]|author=Leeper, Sam|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=December 22, 2012|page=C.9|quote=}}</ref> In the 2012 Proviso West Holiday tournament, Morgan Park defeated a sophomore year [[Jalen Brunson]]-led [[Stevenson High School (Lincolnshire, Illinois)|Stevenson High School]] with Davis defending against Brunson, who posted a game-high 17 in 67–52 game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1265707252|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1265707252}}|title=Morgan Park's collective effort stops Stevenson|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|author=Newton, Jeff|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=December 30, 2012|page=8|quote=}}</ref> On January 5, 2013, they were the number 1 ranked Class 3A school in the state and they defeated the number 3 ranked and junior year [[Keita Bates-Diop]]-led [[University High School (Normal, Illinois)|University High School]] 81–51. Bates had a game-high 20 against Garrett's 19.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1283081287|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1283081287}}|title=No. 3 Pioneersfall to No. 1 team|work=[[The Pantagraph]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=January 6, 2013|page=B.4|quote=}}</ref> When Morgan Park clashed with the senior season Parker/Nunn-led Simeon, there was controversy surrounding ineligibility determinations for 3 Simeon reserve players, including junior [[Donte Ingram]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1269606095|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1269606095}}|title=No time to dwell on 'wrong' ruling|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=January 16, 2013|page=B.4|quote=}}</ref> Despite 23 points by Garrett, Simeon handed Morgan Park its second loss by a 53–51 margin on January 16 at the [[Emil and Patricia Jones Convocation Center]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1270017733|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1270017733}}|title=Surviving the pressure: Wolverines hold off Morgan Park's swarming defense; SIMEON 53, MORGAN PARK 51|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Kane, Colleen|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=January 17, 2013|page=9|quote=}}</ref>

[[File:20130316 IHSA 3A championship game Billy Garrett (3).JPG|thumb|Garrett for [[Morgan Park High School]] in the 2013 [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] 3A championship game.]]
In the 2013 Chicago Public League playoff quarterfinals against a junior season [[Cliff Alexander]]-led number 10-ranked [[Curie Metropolitan High School]] the number 2-ranked Morgan Park needed balanced scoring, including a team-high 15 points from Garrett, and a rally after trailing after each quarter to win 60–58.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1285448995|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1285448995}}|title=Mustangs focus on game, not altercation: Comeback vs. Curie sets up showdown; MORGAN PARK 60, CURIE 58|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=February 11, 2013|page=2|quote=}}</ref> In the semifinals against Simeon, they never trailed in regulation, but still needed an overtime [[layup]] by Garrett with 10 seconds remaining for a 54–53 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1287358158|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1287358158}}|title=MORGAN PARK 54, SIMEON 53 (OT): Patience pays; Garrett, Mustangs get redemption against Wolverines|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=February 14, 2013|page=7|quote=}}</ref> In the championship game against junior season Okafor-led [[Whitney M. Young Magnet High School]], Garrett made 2 free throws with 1:47 remaining to give Morgan Park a three point lead, but their strategy to force someone other than Okafor (who wound up with 19 points and 14 rebounds) to beat them left them vulnerable to a game-tying three-point shot. Then, Garrett was rejected by one of Okafor's 7 blocks to end regulation before they lost 60–56 in overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1288057353|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1288057353}}|title=Making it big: Okafor, Reynolds lead Dolphins to city title; YOUNG 60, MORGAN PARK 56 (OT)|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=February 16, 2013|page=2.6|quote=}}</ref>

In the Class 3A Supersectional game hosted at [[Joliet Central High School]], Morgan Park handily defeated Hillcrest 77–44 on March 12 as Garrett's stat line included just 8 points, 4 assists and 4 steals. This victory qualified them for the final four semifinal competition at [[Carver Arena]] in [[Peoria, Illinois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1316044712|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1316044712}}|title=Mustangs roll behind return of 'old' Davis: 3A MORGAN PARK 77, HILLCREST 44|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 15, 2013|page=8|quote=}}</ref> Garrett entered the semifinals with averages of 17.6 points, 8 assists, and 5 rebounds. The 33-point victory lowered the team's average margin of victory in the 2013 IHSA playoffs to 46.4 (with wins of 67, 33, 63, 36 and 33 points).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1316870386|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1316870386}}|title=Mustangs not letting up: Morgan Park firing on all cylinders heading into semis|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 13, 2013|page=7|quote=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1317108561|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1317108561}}|title=Sixth sense says Simeon will be tough to beat|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 15, 2013|page=7|quote=}}</ref> Morgan Park defeated [[Limestone Community High School District 310]] on March 15 by a 70–49 margin as Davis scored all 15 of his points (including 10–10 free throw shooting) before the fourth quarter.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1317108671|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1317108671}}|title=Changed men: Mustangs dress in hallway, then roll into title game; MORGAN PARK 70, BARTONVILLE LIMESTONE 49|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Narang, Bob|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 16, 2013|page=9|quote=}}</ref><ref name=Box/> As a senior, he led the team to the 2013 [[Illinois High School Association|IHSA]] 3A championship over [[Cahokia High School]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ihsa.org/archive/bkb/2012-13/3bracket.htm|title=Class 3A Boys Basketball Brackets — 2012–13|access-date=May 7, 2019|date=March 18, 2013|publisher=[[Illinois High School Association]]}}</ref><ref name=Box>{{cite web|url=https://www.ihsa.org/Sports-Activities/Boys-Basketball/Records-History|title=Boys Basketball Class 3A State Final Results — 2012–13|access-date=May 7, 2019|date=March 16, 2013|publisher=[[Illinois High School Association]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.pjstar.com/eye/2013/03/16/chicago-morgan-park-wins-the-ihsa-class-3a-championship/|title=Chicago Morgan Park wins the IHSA Class 3A Championship|access-date=May 7, 2019|date=March 16, 2013|work=[[Peoria Journal Star]]}}</ref> The balanced scoring included 4 double-digit scorers as Garrett paced the team with 14 in the 63–48 victory on March 16. Morgan Park finished the season as the IHSA Class 3A champions with a 33–3 record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1317291241|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1317291241}}|title=Morgan Park 63, Cahokia 48|work=[[St. Louis Post-Dispatch]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 17, 2013|page=C.15|quote=}}</ref>

Just before the final four weekend, the Associated Press named its All-state teams, with Garrett as it highest point recipient in Class 3A, where he was accompanied by junior Bates-Diop on the first team. Again most of the future NBA talent was in Class 4A (first team: Parker, Okafor, Hill, Alexander, and Brown; second team: Nunn, [[Tyler Ulis]], and Brunson).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1317120117|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1317120117}}|title=Boys basketball|work=[[Daily Herald (Arlington Heights, Illinois)|Daily Herald]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 15, 2013|page=7|quote=}}</ref> Thus, despite him being atop the 3A talent, the ''Chicago Tribune'' only listed him as second team All-state at the end of March along with Hill, Alvin Ellis, teammate Davis and [[Alec Peters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1321665768|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1321665768}}|title=Second team|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=March 31, 2013|page=13|quote=}}</ref> Following the season Rivals.com listed him 22nd among point guards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1373405622|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1373405622}}|title=Alexander the great: Curie star could be game-changer in DePaul's bid to boost recruiting|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Ryan, Shannon|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=July 3, 2013|page=3.8|quote=}}</ref>

==College career==
[[File:20170213 Villanova-Depaul Billy Garrett moves on Eric Paschall.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Garrett for the [[2016–17 DePaul Blue Demons men's basketball team|2016–17 DePaul Blue Demons]] against [[Eric Paschall]]]]
In January 2014, he nearly died from a sickle cell crisis that caused intense leg pains during a flight and a "near-death experience" at the hospital in [[Newark, New Jersey]] afterwards. Garrett managed to rebound from his attack and win conference rookie of the year honors.<ref name="haugh"/> He missed two games in January and February when his SC form (which is subject to factors such as fatigue, stress, cold, high altitude but is less severe than the SS form) flared up with shooting pain in both of his legs on a flight to New Jersey to play the January 25 game at [[2013–14 Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball team|Seton Hall]]. He also missed the February 1 game against [[2013–14 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1648034881|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1648034881}}|title=Beating tough odds is in Garrett's blood: Sickle cell disease can't derail DePaul sophomore|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Haugh, David|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=January 26, 2015|page=|quote=}}</ref> He averaged 12.4 points and 3.2 assists per game as a freshman.<ref name="si">{{cite magazine|last1=Hamilton|first1=Brian|title=DePaul star freshman Billy Garrett Jr. thrives in defiance of his disease|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/03/06/depaul-blue-demons-billy-garret-jr-sickle-cell-disease|access-date=May 21, 2018|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|date=March 6, 2014}}</ref> As a junior, he averaged 12.6 points, 3.5 assists, and 2.9 rebounds per game on a 9–22 team.<ref name="tide"/>

During his career at DePaul, Garrett led the team in scoring once (2014–15, 12.3), free throw percentage all four season (82.5%, 83.2%, 81.9% and 88.2), and in assists each of his final three seasons (126, 107, 106). His career free throw percentage of 84.1% is third in school history and his single-season percentage of 88.2% (2016–17) is fourth {{as of|November 2022|lc=y}}. He went 11–11 or better from the free throw line on four separate occasions ([[2014–15 St. John's Red Storm men's basketball team|St. John's]] January 18, 2015, 13; [[2015–16 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] January 9, 2016, 12, [[2014–15 Colorado Buffaloes men's basketball team|Colorado]] December 22, 2014, 11 and [[2014–15 Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball team|Milwaukee]] December 7, 2014, 11), whereas no one else in school history has done it more than once. Three of these happenings occurred in the same season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://depaulbluedemons.com/documents/2022/5/19/MBB_AllTimeRecords_2022.pdf|title=DePaul Blue Demons Men's Basketball All-Time Records|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=May 19, 2022|publisher=[[DePaul Blue Demons]]}}</ref> 

He won several games for DePaul at the free throw line at the end of a close game. On January 20, 2016, against [[2015–16 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]] he made a layup followed by a free throw with 1.1 seconds left in a 57–56 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1758341595|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1758341595}}|title=Garrett, Jr.'s and-one puts MU's postseason hopes on life support|agency=[[University Wire]]|author=Reiner, Dan|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=January 20, 2016|page=|quote=}}</ref> 

On January 10, 2017 he made another three point play with 4.7 seconds remaining for a 64–63 victory over [[2016–17 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1858028103|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1858028103}}|title=Demons digging for Big East treasures: After victory vs. Providence, they seek elusive win streak|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=Helfgot, Mike|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=January 13, 2017|page=3|quote=}}</ref> On January 31, against [[2016–17 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] at home at the [[Allstate Arena]], Garrett eclipsed [[Stephen Howard (basketball)|Stephen Howard]]'s career total of 528 made free throws.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/400919703|title=L.J. Peak scores 5 points in final minute to lift Georgetown|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=January 31, 2017|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://depaulbluedemons.com/news/2017/2/1/Garrett_s_DePaul_Journey_Leading_to_Top_of_Record_Books|title=Garrett's DePaul Journey Leading to Top of Record Books|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=February 1, 2017|publisher=[[DePaul Blue Demons]]}}</ref> Against Georgetown on February 22 on the road at the [[Verizon Center (Washington, D.C.)|Verizon Center]] now Capital One Arena, he converted both free throws with 0.2 seconds remaining for a 67–65 victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/1870860559|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|1870860559}}|title=Orange's banked 3 at buzzer beats Duke: Gillon winner ends Blue Devils' streak at 7 straight wins|work=[[Chicago Tribune]]|author=|access-date=February 26, 2024|date=February 23, 2017|page=4|quote=}}</ref>

Regarding the lack of team success, "It has been disappointing for me," Garrett said. "I wanted to come in and help change the culture and bring a positive outlook on DePaul basketball citywide and nationwide."<ref name="tide"/> As a senior, he averaged 14.9 points per game while shooting 36 percent from three.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hudrick|first1=Paul|title=Billy Garrett shares Sixers' desire to win after 4 straight losing seasons at DePaul|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/philadelphia-76ers/billy-garrett-shares-sixers-desire-win-after-4-straight-losing-seasons-depaul|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=June 13, 2017}}</ref> Garrett finished his career as DePaul's all-time leader in made free throws (565).<ref name="stack">{{cite news|last1=Stack|first1=Dan|title=Billy Garrett Jr. chases dream in the G League|url=https://247sports.com/college/depaul/Article/Billy-Garrett-Jr-chases-dream-in-the-G-League-114905069|access-date=May 21, 2018|work=247 Sports|date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Westchester Knicks (2017–2019)===
After going undrafted in the [[2017 NBA draft]], Garrett did not play in the NBA Summer League. He joined the [[Westchester Knicks]] of the NBA G-League. Garrett increased his role on the team after [[Trey Burke]] was called up to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref name="stack"/> Garrett averaged 11.9 points, 2.7 boards, 2.5 assists and 1.0 steals in 27.1 minutes per game in his first season with the team. He appeared in all 50 games, making 14 starts. On October 4, 2018, he signed an Exhibit 10 deal with the [[New York Knicks]] to participate in the team's 2018 [[training camp]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Knicks' Billy Garrett: Signing with Knicks |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/knicks-billy-garrett-signing-with-knicks/ |access-date=October 4, 2018 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 4, 2018}}</ref> He returned to Westchester to play a second season for coach [[Mike Miller (basketball, born 1964)|Mike Miller]], averaging 16.5 points, 3.8 assists, and 3.2 rebounds per game in 48 games played (32 starts). He posted a 31.6% three-point field goal percentage and an 85.6% free throw percentage. In his two seasons with the Westchester Knicks, he became the franchise's all-time leader in points, field goals made, assists, minutes played and games played.<ref name=BGI1CwNYK/>

===New York Knicks (2019)===
On April 2, 2019, the [[New York Knicks]] announced that they had signed Garrett to a 10-day contract.<ref name=BGI1CwNYK>{{cite web|title=Billy Garrett Inks 10-Day Contract with New York Knicks|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/billy-garrett-inks-10-day-contract-with-new-york-knicks/|date=April 2, 2019|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 2, 2019|archive-date=April 3, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403150108/https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/billy-garrett-inks-10-day-contract-with-new-york-knicks/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Knicks roster was beset with numerous injuries ([[Kadeem Allen]] (concussion), [[Isaiah Hicks]] (sore left hip), [[Dennis Smith Jr.]] (sore lower back), [[Allonzo Trier]] (strained left calf) and [[Noah Vonleh]] (sprained right ankle)),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071857|title=Harden scores 26 in Rockets' 120-96 blowout win over Knicks|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=April 5, 2019|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> and Garrett's G League season had just come to an end.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2209771346|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2209771346}}|title=Billy Garrett Jr. reaches NBA, reflects on DePaul|agency=[[University Wire]]|author=Kreymer, Lawrence|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=April 15, 2019|page=|quote=}}</ref> He debuted in the NBA on April 3 for the [[2018-19 New York Knicks season|New York Knicks]] on the road against [[2018-19 Orlando Magic season|Orlando]] with 4 points in 11 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2202716755|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2202716755}}|title=HEZONJA GETS TO SHOW HIS MAGIC TOUCH: Knick scores 29 points in loss to club where he began NBA career|work=[[Newsday]]|author=Popper, Steve|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=April 4, 2019|page=55|quote=}}</ref> [[Emmanuel Mudiay]] and [[Frank Ntilikina]] also were unavailable during his tenure leaving Garrett as the only true point guard on the roster at one point.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2203612057|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2203612057}}|title=Mario's rating: PG: Hurting Knicks start Hezonja at point guard|work=[[Newsday]]|author=Popper, Steve|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=April 6, 2019|page=29|quote=}}</ref> In his brief NBA tenure to close out the [[2018-19 NBA season]], he was able to play at the [[United Center]] in his hometown when the Knicks played the [[2018-19 Chicago Bulls season|Bulls]] on April 9.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401071886|title=Knicks top Bulls 96-86, avoid new franchise low for wins|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=April 9, 2019|agency=[[Associated Press]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Several of his NBA career highs (8 points, 2 rebounds, 2 assists and 4 field goals) were tallied or tied at the United Center in his only NBA win. Garrett made all four of his free throw attempts, but missed all eight of his three-point shot attempts in the NBA.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/3059356/billy-garrett-jr|title=BILLY GARRETT JR.: Game logs|access-date=February 27, 2024|publisher=[[ESPPN]]}}</ref> He became the first NBA player known to have the sickle-cell disease, which boosted his profile as an inspirational advocate for the affliction. In four games, he averaged 6.5 points per game.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Price |first1=Khobi |title=Billy Garrett Jr., the only NBA player with sickle cell disease, is an inspiration |url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/2019/7/24/20727050/billy-garrett-sickle-cell-disease-inspiration-knicks-depaul-morgan-park |access-date=January 4, 2020 |work=[[Chicago Sun Times]] |date=July 24, 2019}}</ref> In July 2019, Garrett joined the [[Phoenix Suns]] for the 2019 [[NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Cunningham |first1=Cody |title=Lecque Hits Game-Winning Free Throws as Suns Defeat Spurs |url=https://www.nba.com/suns/postgame/lecque-hits-game-winning-free-throws-suns-defeat-spurs# |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 4, 2020 |date=July 10, 2019}}</ref> In August, his returning player rights were traded to the [[Maine Red Claws]] for [[Andrew White (basketball)|Andrew White]]'s returning player rights.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/2282329277|url-access=subscription|id={{ProQuest|2282329277}}|title=Thursday's Sports Digest: Kannegieser wins Match Play title in playoff|work=[[Sun Journal (Lewiston, Maine)|Sun Journal]]|author=|access-date=February 27, 2024|date=August 29, 2019|page=|quote=}}</ref>
